correctness.rationale: For a failed initial filled set, skew closure ends with a nonempty skew-stalled white residue; conversely the complement of a stalled white set is failed. Thus the extremal problem is exactly minimum stalled-white size. Connectedness excludes size one. A size-two stalled set would be a nonadjacent open-twin pair, but singleton zero-block threshold graphs have strictly nested open neighborhoods on their independent-side vertices. For a stalled triple, choosing the largest represented one-block forces at least two white vertices in that block; the third must lie in the same block or earlier in the creation order. Every such triple is directly checked to be stalled. Counting these disjoint forms gives the stated formula. The packaged verifier independently replays all eligible profiles through order 11, including every initial filled set; finite verification is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The class is mathematically natural: singleton canonical zero-blocks are exactly the threshold-side boundary where the immediate two-vertex false-twin stalled obstruction disappears. The theorem identifies the next obstruction size, gives all extremal obstructions, and counts every maximum failed set. This is more than a routine parameter substitution: it converts an NP-complete general decision problem into a closed-form structural theorem on a canonical graph class and answers an explicit later-literature question about counting maximum failed sets for an infinite family.
